note:
415 -> 405, and the whole of the -10 is real element types replacing inference mypy could not make.

Measured the way py_typecheck.yml prescribes: mypy 2.3.0 and NOTHING ELSE in the venv, --no-incremental, `-p odoo.tools`, in a `git archive` tree of HEAD plus this change. Two consecutive runs, 405 both times.

WHAT MOVED. Thirty-five `var-annotated` sites said only that mypy could not infer an element type from an empty literal. Seventeen of them are now annotated, in the seven modules this branch already had open:

  view_validation  _validators (view tag -> its predicates), _relaxng_cache
  cache            class_slots
  config           _log_entries, _warn_entries
  convert          res, sub_records, _sequences
  profiler         SyncCollector.post_process stack, QwebCollector.events,
                   QwebCollector.post_process stack/results/archs
  mixin_profiler   lines
  translate        expressions, grouped_rows, occurrences, result, terms,
                   xml_defined, records_per_model, imported_langs, rows_by_id,
                   python_translations, web_translations

AN ANNOTATION IS NOT FREE, AND ONE OF THESE PROVED IT. Annotating the translate.py batch first took the count UP, 445 -> 458 in the project venv: a real element type lets mypy check the uses, and `grouped_rows` had been guessed as `dict[tuple, list]` when the body builds a nested dict through `setdefault(src, {})` and then calls `.setdefault`/`.get` on the value. The guess was wrong, and it was the annotation that said so. Corrected to `dict[str, dict[str, Any]]`, the batch nets to zero on its own -- ten `var-annotated` removed, ten genuine errors exposed underneath -- and the -10 in this floor is the other six modules.

That is the argument for annotating from the body rather than from mypy `hint:` text: the hint offers `list[<type>]` for anything empty, and taking it on faith buys a smaller number and a false statement.
